messages:
Anya: Quick follow-up on the safetensors -> streaming adapter cleanup. I'd like to propose we simplify the loader interface to a small pull-based API that yields shards/chunks and provides manifest hints (shape, dtype, shard-order). This would remove the two-layer adapter we have now. Thoughts?

Matt: Curious about warmup implications. If adapter is pull-based, where do prefetch/warmup hooks live? inside the runtime or the loader? :thinking:

Anya: My thinking: loader exposes async iterator that yields ShardChunks and optional warmup hint objects. Runtime owns scheduling and warmup queues. Keeps runtime-only policies out of loaders and keeps loader simple.

Diego: Two concerns: 1) sharded/safetensors with non-contiguous mmap-backed tensors — pulling chunks might force copies or remaps. 2) how to express "this shard must be hot-started" vs optional prefetch.

Sophie: +1 for simple iterator. For the hot-start semantics we could add a small enum in the hint: {priority: high|low|background, checksum, expected_lifetime}

Anya: Example sketch:

```
interface ShardChunk {
  id: string
  offset: number
  length: number
  kind: 'tensor'|'metadata'
  reader: () => Promise<ArrayBuffer> // or zero-copy view
}

async function* loadModel(manifest){
  yield {chunk, hint: {priority:'high'}}
}
```

Liam: Perf-wise we need a way for reader() to return a zero-copy mmap view on platforms that support it, and a fallback that yields a pooled buffer otherwise. Also we should avoid per-chunk allocations.

Diego: For safetensors bundles we could expose a small file-backed view type that wraps a file descriptor + offset/len. That makes zero-copy possible for the on-prem private deployment.

Matt: Is this compatible with existing manifest-first warmup we use on Dedicated? We still need the ability to say "index-first then stream" vs "stream-only".

Sophie: We can keep manifest mode as a manifest-only loader that yields priority high for all index entries. Stream-only will yield as it sees shards. So the runtime policy stays the same.

Anya: Backwards compat: keep old adapter in the codebase for a deprecation cycle but default new codepaths to iterator. Migration plan: 1) implement iterator in safetensors loader; 2) enable in canary for small models; 3) measure warmup coverage and RSS behavior.

Liam: Add perf counters: chunk-read latency, zero-copy hit rate, prefetch queue fill. Also add a load-failure fallback that retries N times and falls back to slower copy path.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/safetensors-adapter-v2 -> eng-ml-canary at 2024-09-15T18:00Z :rocket:

Matt: One more edge: partial-shard eviction during OOM. If runtime evicts a partially-warmed shard, loader must be resumable (able to yield remaining bytes). That implies deterministic chunk boundaries.

Anya: Agree. We'll define chunk boundaries in the manifest (start/len) and make readers idempotent. Ok I'll open a short RFC with the interface sketch and a migration checklist.

Sophie: please add a section on security: signed manifests and checksum verification for private deploys.

Diego: Also add a small note about sstensor index format versions and compatibility.

Anya: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
